trick: Checkpoint rewind: restore the code but keep the conversation
source_quote: "**Restore code**: revert file changes while keeping the conversation" vs "**Restore code and conversation**: revert both code and conversation to that point" (Claude Code checkpointing docs); best practices: "That makes it low-risk to try the bolder approach first and rewind if it doesn't work out."
source_note: Approved by Sebi 4 Nov 2026 (PROTOCOL.md). Module 6 rules = private/m5/RULES.md 'Runs' section: one project (the M6 fixture, being built in parallel; base set 4 Nov from the built fixture), Haiku 4.5, 18 runs a side, three numbers recorded before each run (pass rate = all four traps D1-D4 + core from the grader's `BUGS` line, the behaviour count below, cost per passed run), the habit measured on the plain side first, an agent reads every transcript. allowed_tools_extra mirrors Module 5 and is re-aligned to the fixture's real test command before the run. Design rationale and kill switches: private/m6/DESIGN.md. `when: "fails"` is a runner field (harness/run.py, 4 Nov 2026): before the turn the runner grades an APFS clone of the repo with the task's own hidden grader, records {attempt, passed, BUGS line} in the raw row, and skips this and every later turn if it passed. The agent never sees the grader or its output, only the fixed retry line: the stand-in for a user who tried the fix and says it is still broken.
side_env_note: Both sides set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING=true (found in Claude Code 2.1.309: headless file checkpoints are off unless this is set). Rewind is the hidden headless flag `claude --resume <id> --rewind-files <user-message-uuid>` (2.1.309 help text: 'Restore files to state at the specified user message and exit (requires --resume)'), not yet dry-run in this lab.
harness_needs: turn.rewind_files = true (standalone `claude --resume <sid> --rewind-files <uuid of the first user message>` before the turn; uuid read from the session file in the lab config dir)
fallback if rewind-files fails the dry run: turn.reset = true (git), reported as such
behaviour_count: Among runs whose attempt 1 failed: retry passes per side; plus retries whose first edit repeats attempt 1's edited files (the kept chat should steer away) and files left un-restored because only Bash changed them (rewind's documented gap)
habit_measure: Plain re-roll rate: the without side IS a clean re-send of the task (what 'Restore code and conversation' leaves you), so its retry pass rate is the habit baseline
anchor: Rewound code with the chat kept: N of S second tries passed; rewound both: M of S

with.label: Attempt 1 fails: Restore code (rewind files), keep the conversation, one retry

turns.prompt: That didn't fix it, so I've rewound your code changes. Try again.

without.label: Attempt 1 fails: Restore code and conversation (rewind files, fresh session), re-send the task

turns.prompt:
{task}

An earlier attempt at this didn't fix it, and its code changes have been rewound. Try again.
